info.title: Music Nerd API: artist chat
info.description: A listener's conversation about one artist, answered from the artist's approved sources and the web and streamed as it is written. Each request counts against the same allowance as [Ask about an artist](/api-reference/research/ask-artist): 30 questions per visitor per hour (per account with a token, per IP without) and 200 across the site over a rolling 24 hours.

post.description: Answers the last user message about this artist, using earlier messages as context, and streams the reply as an [AI SDK UI message stream](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot): tool steps as the model searches and reads sources, a `source-url` part for each source it read, and the answer text citing them as `[n]`. No credentials are needed; an optional Privy `Authorization: Bearer` token makes the hourly allowance follow the account instead of the caller's IP.

parts.text: Where did Bio Ritmo record their latest album?

200.description:
The reply, streamed as server-sent events in the AI SDK UI message stream protocol. Read it with `useChat` from `@ai-sdk/react` and a `DefaultChatTransport` pointed at this endpoint ([chatbot guide](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot)); the assistant message's `parts` then hold:

- **Tool steps** `tool-searchSources`, `tool-readSource` and `tool-webSearch`, each moving from `input-available` to `output-available`. Show them as progress, for example "Searching saved sources…", "Reading richmondfolkfestival.org…", "Searching the web…". Outputs: `searchSources` → `{ sources: [{ sourceId, title, url, snippet }] }` (up to 8 saved sources); `readSource` → `{ n, title, url, text }`, or `{ error }` for an unknown `sourceId`; `webSearch` → `{ results: [{ n, title, url, snippet }] }`.
- **`source-url`** `{ sourceId, url, title }`, once per distinct source: on a saved source's first read, and for each web search result. `sourceId` is `"1"`, `"2"`, … in order. `title` is the host name for a saved source (saved sources keep no page title) and the result's title for a web result.
- **`text`**, the answer. It cites sources inline as `[n]`, matching a `source-url` part's `sourceId`, and says plainly when the sources don't answer the question.

On the wire each event is a `data:` line holding one JSON chunk, ending with `data: [DONE]`:

- `start`: the reply begins (`messageId`).
- `start-step` / `finish-step`: one model step begins / ends; a reply takes up to 6.
- `tool-input-start`: a tool call begins (`toolCallId`, `toolName`).
- `tool-input-delta`: a piece of the tool call's JSON input as the model writes it (`inputTextDelta`).
- `tool-input-available` / `tool-output-available`: the call's full `input` / its `output`.
- `source-url`: a citable source, as above.
- `text-start`, `text-delta` (`delta`), `text-end`: the answer text.
- `finish`: the reply is done (`finishReason`).

400.description: The artist ID is not a UUID, the body is not JSON, `messages` is empty, the last message is not a `user` message with a non-empty text part, or that question is over 500 characters. Only the last 12 messages are read; earlier ones are ignored.

429.description: The question allowance is spent. `code` names it: `visitor_question_quota` (30 questions per visitor per hour) or `question_planning_quota` (200 across the site per rolling day).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the quota window resets, only when the response carries `retryAfterSeconds`.

X-MusicNerd-Quota.description: `true` on a quota response, so a client can tell it from a transient 429.

value.error: You've reached your question limit for this hour. Try again in 42 minutes.
Music Nerd has reached its daily chat allowance. Try again in 3 minutes.

privyBearer.description: Optional. The signed-in user's access token, so the allowance counts per account. Copy it at https://musicnerd.net/access after signing in.

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first, as AI SDK `UIMessage`s; `useChat` sends this for you. The last message is the question; at most the last 12 are read.

parts.description: Message parts. Only `text` parts `{ "type": "text", "text": "…" }` are read; tool, source and other parts the client echoes back are accepted and ignored.
